title: Eliminating an invariant order on bounded-degree structures
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: For every finite relational vocabulary tau, every integer D≥0 and every globally order-invariant first-order sentence phi over tau together with an extra binary relation <, does there exist an FO(tau) sentence psi equivalent to phi on every finite nonempty tau-structure of Gaifman degree at most D?
definitions:
A finite relational vocabulary lists relation symbols and their finite arities; equality is logical and there are no function symbols. The Gaifman graph has the structure’s elements as vertices. Two distinct elements are adjacent when they occur together in a tuple of any input relation. Degree counts distinct neighbors and excludes the auxiliary order. The bound D is fixed independently of the size of a structure.

Global order invariance means that for every finite tau-structure A and every two linear orders on its domain, phi has the same truth value in the two expansions. The conclusion asks for a single sentence psi, depending only on tau, D and phi, which agrees with that value on every A of degree at most D. There is no size bound or computable translation requirement. Quantifying over the whole degree-D class also yields the conclusion for each subclass. The selected convention is global invariance, rather than a promise of invariance only on one chosen subclass. Full first-order syntax is allowed, with arbitrary quantifier alternation.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of this expressive collapse, or a vocabulary, degree bound and globally invariant sentence for which no ordinary first-order sentence works on the entire bounded-degree class. Collapse for a restricted syntactic fragment alone does not meet the target.
context:
Bounded degree controls the local neighborhoods available to first-order formulas. The question asks whether an auxiliary order can nevertheless define additional queries.

The cluster fragment has a collapse theorem, but the unrestricted first-order question is broader.
why: The collapse would show that auxiliary order adds no expressive power in a broad sparse setting.

import_provenance.original_title: Eliminating an invariant order on bounded-degree structures
import_provenance.original_statement: On every class of finite relational structures of bounded Gaifman degree, is each order-invariant first-order sentence equivalent to an ordinary first-order sentence? This asks whether an arbitrary auxiliary order adds any expressive power even on locally sparse structures, continuing Schweikardt’s work on invariant logics.
